walkthrough: Identify the nucleons in $^{3}_{1}\text{H}$: proton number $Z=1$ gives $1$ proton, and neutrons $= A-Z = 3-1 = 2$ neutrons.
State the quark rule: proton $= uud$ so $2$ up and $1$ down, neutron $= udd$ so $1$ up and $2$ down.
Count up quarks: from $1$ proton $1 \times 2 = 2$, from $2$ neutrons $2 \times 1 = 2$, total $2+2 = 4$ up quarks.
Count down quarks: from $1$ proton $1 \times 1 = 1$, from $2$ neutrons $2 \times 2 = 4$, total $1+4 = 5$ down quarks.
Check charge: $(4 \times +2/3) + (5 \times -1/3) = +1$, matching a hydrogen nucleus with $Z=1$. This is option A.
